description: The thermostat never starts (it has a lockout, or its own sensor reads warm). The loop steps 66 -> 68 -> 70 and then STOPS at the +4 F cap for the next two hours, though the bedroom stays at 58 F.

events.note: The hallway thermostat's own sensor: satisfied, so it will not start by itself.
Day classification (cold: heat all night / hot: cool all night).
Bedtime: the sleep band is written and the sleep window (remote sensor in use) begins.
Still cold; the thermostat never started.

assertions.reason: Two steps (after the 300 s startup wait) reach the +4 F cap (70) and then STOP: an hour and a half of a cold bedroom never writes 72.
The thermostat is held at target + 4 F, never more.

notes: Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md section 10), Issue #1194 increment (e). Tier A: the real ClimateAdvisorCoordinator + AutomationEngine under FakeHass/FakeScheduler (use_coordinator=true, so the sleep-sensor listener and the 1-minute timer are real); every assertion is track=integration for that reason and is evaluated, not skipped.

(a) Effectiveness: scratch-copy mutation run of this scenario against the production code (worktree untouched). It FAILS when M01: the whole offset deleted (the write path adds 0 and the check is a no-op); M02: the +4 F cap removed. Passes unmutated.
(b) Docs <-> production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md 'Remote-sensor outer loop on the thermostat setpoint (Issue #1194, increment a)': 'Caps (the tighter wins)'. Matches production.

(c) Occupant outcome if this regressed: Without the cap a thermostat that ignores the loop would be driven to its maximum setpoint and the whole house, not the bedroom, would overheat the moment it did start.

verdict.summary: The +4 F cap: the loop never asks the thermostat for more than target + 4 F.
verdict.observed_behavior: Writes: 66, 68 (after 1 min), 70 (after the 300 s startup wait), then none.
verdict.expected_behavior: At most +4 F beyond the target in the gap direction.
